sections.title: Introduction to the Letter
observations: The Apostle Paul begins his letter to the Corinthians by establishing his authority as an apostle of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that his calling is not from men but from God, which sets the tone for the entire letter.
Paul addresses the church in Corinth, a city known for its diversity and moral challenges, and he expresses gratitude for the grace given to them in Christ.

sections.title: Divisions in the Church
observations: Paul confronts the issue of divisions within the Corinthian church. He hears reports that members are aligning themselves with different leaders, such as Paul, Apollos, and Cephas, which undermines the unity that should exist in Christ.
He emphasizes that Christ is not divided and that the church should not be divided over human leaders. This call for unity is a central theme in Paul's message.

sections.title: The Wisdom of God vs. the Wisdom of the World
observations: Paul contrasts the wisdom of God with the wisdom of the world. He points out that the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing but is the power of God to those who are being saved.
This section highlights the paradox of the Christian faith, where what seems weak and foolish to the world is actually the means of salvation.

sections.title: God's Choice of the Weak and Foolish
observations: Paul explains that God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise and the weak things to shame the strong. This serves to demonstrate that salvation is entirely a work of God and not based on human merit.
He reminds the Corinthians that many of them were not wise, powerful, or noble by worldly standards when they were called, emphasizing God's grace in their selection.

importantVerses.commentary: I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same judgment.
For the word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong.

questions: What does Paul mean by calling for unity among the believers in Corinth?
How does the concept of the 'foolishness' of the cross challenge our understanding of wisdom?
In what ways does God's choice of the weak and foolish encourage us in our own faith journey?
